title: KV: Age-based demotion with reservation smoothing and background page advection
author: Maya Chen
description:
Motivation: Large production workloads showed periodic tail-latency spikes and increased spill events under mixed tenant workloads where short-lived prefixes competed with long-running chat sessions. Previous heuristics (pure LRU or simple frequency counters) responded poorly to sudden workload shifts and produced fragmentation that amplified spill overhead. This change introduces an age-based demotion layer that cooperates with tenant reservations and a light-weight background page advection pass to improve memory residency decisions and reduce spill churn.

What this PR does (summary): - Implements an AgeDemoter that maintains compact per-segment age histograms (exponentially decayed) to identify stable cold ranges. - Adds a reservation-aware admission threshold: tenants with active reservations retain higher soft residency quotas, while bursty tenants see steeper demotion curves. - Background page advection: a low-priority sweeper migrates scattered hot lines into compacted subpages to lower fragmentation before eviction. - Spill smoothing: when spillback is triggered, the system emits a paced spill schedule to avoid synchronous spikes. - Integration points for the scheduler and kernel selection: demoter exposes hint bits used by the serving runtime kernel selection to prefer quantized-backed execution on pages with high churn.

Design notes: - Age histogram per allocation-span uses 8 buckets (log-decayed) to keep memory overhead < 0.5% of KV heap. Histograms are updated on hot-paths with an atomic sampled increment to avoid writer contention. - Demotion policy computes a demotion_score = alpha * age_weight + beta * eviction_pressure - gamma * reservation_boost; coefficients are tuned via feature flag. - Reservation smoothing: reservations expose a moving-average usage signal to soften abrupt quota drops; this reduces oscillation and prevents cache thrashing during autoscale events. - Background advection runs at cgroup-priority and operates on cold candidates only; it performs in-place compaction where possible and fallbacks to lightweight copy if necessary. - Spill pacing uses token-bucket per-tenant combined with global spill-backpressure signal so that downstream storage is not overloaded.

Checklist: - [x] Design doc added (docs/notes/kv-age-demoter.md) - [x] Unit tests for histogram updates and demotion logic - [x] Integration tests in perf-canary harness - [x] Feature-flag gated rollout with default off - [x] Backwards compatibility: when feature flag is off, system behaves as before

Testing and verification: - Unit/integration: added 28 new unit tests and 4 integration scenarios covering reservation interactions, histogram decay, and advection correctness. - Perf canary: ran against the benchmark-lab mixed-chat workload for 48 hours. Compared to baseline: median p95 latency down 12%, p99 down 18%, spill events per hour reduced from 42 -> 9. Sustained throughput improved by 6% under 70th percentile CPU pressure. - Fault injection: simulated node reclaim & rapid tenant burst; demoter prevented immediate full-scale eviction and smoothed spill incrementally.

Rollout plan: - Feature flag default off; enable in shadow mode for 1 week on a dedicated fleet. - Observe per-tenant spill counts, compaction CPU, and latency SLOs. - Gradual ramp to 25%, 50%, 100% with automatic rollback if spill count increases > 25% or p99 latency regresses by >10%.

Risks and mitigations: - Additional CPU for background advection: capped to 2% of a host core and runs at low priority. - Histogram overhead: compact representation and sampling to limit cost. - Interactions with other evictors: demoter outputs a stable score; existing eviction pipeline consumes scores as hints, not authoritative commands.

Related work: builds on eviction telemetry from ENG-4027 and complements recent slab compaction work; intended to reduce reliance on aggressive spill triggers while improving long-term fragmentation behavior.

release_notes: Improves KV memory management by adding an age-based demotion layer, reservation-aware admission smoothing, and a background page advection worker; reduces spill events and lowers tail latency under mixed workloads. Feature-flag gated; default off.
